newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz to present election bill.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz to present election bill.

text.p: Turkey's new Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz is to present a bill on early elections to parliament soon, a deputy from his party said on Friday.
"In the coming days, a law will be delivered to parliament and preparations for elections will be included in this law," Motherland Party MP Zeki Cakan told reporters.
The left-right coalition under Yilmaz came to power last week after months of political instability under the previous Islamist-led government.
Yilmaz previously indicated he would seek polls in the spring of 1998, but no mention of elections was made in the government programme debated in parliament this week.

"An election date will be determined according to the conditions of the day," Cakan said. Elections are due in the year 2000, but a key left-wing party supporting the coalition has demanded early polls as a condition for its support.
Cakan told a news conference the secularist government would win a confidence vote in parliament on Saturday by a clear margin.

Yilmaz has on paper around 15 votes more than needed to win the vote in the 550-seat assembly and was boosted on Friday by the latest in a series of resignations from a rival opposition conservative party.
